title: Proposal: formnosubmit attribute for active but non-submitted form controls

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

There is no native way to **keep a named form control active** for client-side use (JavaScript) **while excluding it from form submission**. For example, a checkbox used to toggle a UI panel should not be submitted to the server, but must remain interactive and named for frontend logic. Current workarounds force developers to choose between semantic HTML and practical UX needs.

### What solutions exist today?

**disabled attribute**: Excludes the field from submission, but also visually disables it (not suitable for interactive UI elements).

**Place the field outside form**: Loses native form association (form= attribute, validation, or styling).

**JavaScript filtering**: Manually remove the field from FormData before submission (formData.delete('fieldName')), which adds unnecessary complexity and maintenance overhead.


### How would you solve it?

Add a boolean attribute formnosubmit (inspired by the existing formnovalidate attribute available on submit button) to form controls (input, select, textarea). When present:

- The control retains its name and remains fully interactive for JavaScript/CSS.
- It is excluded from the FormData during form submission.

**Example :**

```
<form id="settings">
  <input type="text" name="username"> <!-- Submitted -->
  <input type="checkbox" name="uiToggle" formnosubmit> <!-- Not submitted -->
</form>
<script>
  // Still accessible in JS:
  console.log(document.querySelector('[name="uiToggle"]').checked);
</script>
```


### Anything else?

**Impact**: No breaking changes (older browsers ignore unknown attributes). Reduces reliance on JavaScript for common patterns.
**Use cases**: Client-side toggles, dynamic filters, or any field used only for frontend logic
